poc_summary: reporter-adapted C++ libcurl client (reporter_adapted.cc) drives a multiplexed HTTP/2 TLS download against a local python test server (http2_pause_server.py) that serves a 16MiB body while the client repeatedly pauses/resumes a transfer under backpressure (GH16955_SLOW_MIB=16, GH16955_PAUSE_KIB=1024, GH16955_RESUME_MS=50, GH16955_PAUSE_LIMIT=1). The server/classify.py oracle records how many of the 16MiB slow-stream bytes were actually delivered, the final HTTP/2 peer window, and the count of stream WINDOW_UPDATE frames seen, emitting a single ORACLE_RESULT line.
explanation: Same run.sh / same client+server/classify oracle executed unmodified against all three builds. pre_intro (279a4772ae67) and post_benign (fix 5fbd78eb2dc4 applied) both complete the full 16MiB transfer with peer window restored to 4194304 and 3 stream WINDOW_UPDATEs (ORACLE_RESULT=FULL_16M_RESPONSE, exit 0). post_intro (f78700814d70) stalls permanently after only 10485760 of 16777216 bytes with peer window stuck at 0 and only 1 WINDOW_UPDATE ever sent (ORACLE_RESULT=WINDOW_STALL_10M_ZERO_WINDOW_NO_UPDATE, exit 1), i.e. the HTTP/2 receive-window deadlock after pause/unpause described in GH-16955 and meta.json's root cause (write_paused bridge shrinks the local window to zero; on unpause the window-update submission omits the nghttp2 internal local-window setter call, so the stream never recovers). This is a clean behavioral reproduction: identical invocation, divergent outcome only in post_intro, restored in post_benign.

oracle.description: classify.py compares the HTTP/2 stream's delivered byte count against the configured slow-stream target (16MiB), the final client-observed peer flow-control window, and the number of WINDOW_UPDATE frames issued for that stream, then emits one of two outcome lines: FULL_16M_RESPONSE (transfer completed, window replenished) or WINDOW_STALL_10M_ZERO_WINDOW_NO_UPDATE (transfer permanently stuck at the first 10MiB chunk boundary with a zero window and no further update) — directly reflecting whether the local HTTP/2 receive window was correctly re-opened after pause/resume.
